comparison: Both strongly support the laminar distribution findings for GABA+ and PV+ cells (C46-C58). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and internal consistency, while peer reviewers explicitly valued this as an independent contribution with one noting it 'may prove valuable to researchers.'

Both support the species comparison data (C59-C62, C119). OpenEval notes reliance on single published mouse source, while peer reviewers found the comparative analysis valuable without raising concerns about the mouse data citations.

Both support the double-labeling quantification (C63-C66, C35). OpenEval highlights clear percentages and direct measurements, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings as part of the valuable characterization of marmoset V1.

Both support the primate/rodent comparisons (C67, C116-C118). OpenEval notes potential methodological variability between macaque studies not fully addressed, while peer reviewers accepted these comparative findings without concern.

Both rate as UNCERTAIN due to single injection per serotype (C68-C72). OpenEval emphasizes inability to distinguish serotype differences from injection variability, while peer reviewers stated 'observations with an n = 1 cannot be considered reliable' and noted 'many variables can contribute to success or failure.'

Both rate as UNCERTAIN for statistical comparisons of viral expression patterns (C73-C78). OpenEval notes limitations from single injections despite appropriate statistical tests, while peer reviewers questioned which results 'would hold up had a larger number of injections been made.'

Both rate as UNCERTAIN for specificity measurements (C79-C83, C123-C124). OpenEval highlights high variability and single injection limitation, while peer reviewers noted the 'data set is small' and reliability concerns with n=1 per serotype.

Both rate as UNCERTAIN for coverage measurements (C84-C88, C125). OpenEval notes striking differences but limited confidence from single injections, while peer reviewers expressed uncertainty about reproducibility with larger sample sizes.

OpenEval rates UNSUPPORTED while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for serotype recommendations (C89-C90). OpenEval considers recommendations premature without replication, while peer reviewers noted after revision that 'new language to qualify the strength of evidence' was appropriate, suggesting authors acknowledged limitations.

Both support the injection volume comparison findings (C91-C95). OpenEval emphasizes adequate replication (n=8-12 ROIs) and clear dose-dependent effects, while peer reviewers explicitly validated the S5E2 enhancer utility for PV-selective expression without raising concerns.

Both support the practical recommendation for 180 nl volumes (C96). OpenEval notes it represents interpolation rather than direct testing, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the validated characterization of the S5E2 tool.

Both strongly support the immunoreactivity reduction findings (C97-C108). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate statistics and adequate sample sizes, while peer reviewers explicitly highlighted this as 'a strength of this study' and 'an important observation' about marker gene detection following AAV injections.

Both support the inference about artifactually lowered specificity (C100). OpenEval considers the reasoning sound and important for interpretation, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted this as part of the valuable methodological contribution regarding marker expression.

OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting inconsistency between stated specificity values (91-94% in C8-C10, C109) and detailed data showing maximum 82.3%, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to small sample size but did not specifically flag the numerical discrepancy.

Both support the PV-AAV summary findings (C11-C12, C36-C37, C110). OpenEval confirms consistency with detailed data, while peer reviewers explicitly stated the study 'validate[s] the utility of S5E2 as a PV-selective enhancer in NHPs' and praised the careful characterization.

Both support the overall conclusion about tool utility (C13, C111). OpenEval considers conclusion reasonable given demonstrated values and functional validation, while peer reviewers affirmed 'this goal was achieved' and the study 'provides a valuable guide for other investigators.'

Both support the finding of similarity between viral expression and IHC laminar distributions (C32). OpenEval notes this provides important evidence for viral specificity with serotype variation, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted this as central to validating the viral tools.

OpenEval rates the speculative mechanism for immunoreactivity reduction (C127) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is plausible but unvalidated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval supports the literature citations on species differences (C112-C115, C120-C122) as appropriate for contextualizing findings. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these citation claims, though they accepted the comparative analysis overall.

OpenEval supports the citation on viral effects on gene expression (C126) as providing relevant context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this literature citation.

OpenEval supports the experimental design and methods description (C30-C31, C38-C44, C128-C131), noting clear documentation but limited replication for GABA-AAV serotypes. Peer reviewers raised concerns about sample size but did not separately evaluate the methods documentation claims.
OpenEval supports the methodological validation of PV-IHC for layer identification (C45). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this validation finding.

OpenEval supports the citation of functional validation from Vafaei et al. 2024 (C132). No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this external functional validation citation.
